data.name: Mos2114
data.value: MOS 2114 - 1024x4-bit static RAM. Used in early Commodore machines as color RAM: only the low 4 bits of each addressed cell are wired up, so every byte read or written is masked to a nibble - the upper 4 bits simply don't exist in hardware.

data.name: Mos6522
data.value: MOS 6522 VIA (Versatile Interface Adapter) - general-purpose I/O: two independent 8-bit parallel ports (A/B), each with its own data-direction register; two 16-bit interval timers (one-shot or free-running, Timer 2 also countable via CB1 pulses); an 8-bit shift register; and four handshake/control lines (CA1, CA2, CB1, CB2) that can also raise interrupts. Used throughout the PET/VIC-20/C64 family for keyboard scanning, IEEE-488, cassette motor/sense, and user-port I/O.

data.name: Mos6560
data.value: MOS 6560/6561 VIC ("VIC-I") - the VIC-20's combined video and sound chip. Generates NTSC/PAL composite video directly from character-cell screen RAM (with an optional 2-bit-per-pixel multicolor mode), and drives 3 independent square-wave tone oscillators plus a noise generator through one shared volume register. Has no hardware sprite unit at all - hardware sprites are a later chip, the VIC-II used in the Commodore 64, not this one.

data.name: Mt6520
data.value: MOS/MDA 6520 PIA (Peripheral Interface Adapter) - two independent 8-bit parallel ports (A/B), each with its own data-direction register and two control lines (CA1/CA2, CB1/CB2) for handshaking and interrupt generation on edge transitions. The simpler, earlier sibling of the VIA: no built-in timers and no shift register, just parallel I/O with handshaking.

data.name: Mt6545
data.value: Motorola 6845-compatible CRTC (Cathode Ray Tube Controller) - generates character-based video timing and addressing: horizontal/vertical sync pulses, the scanning address fed to external character-ROM/screen-RAM hardware, and cursor position/shape. It holds no pixel data itself - a pure timing and addressing generator, its 18 internal registers selected through one index/data port pair (write the register index, then read or write its value).
